title: Written standards, enforced
outcome: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is established based on organizational context, cybersecurity strategy, and priorities and is communicated and enforced
why: Written standards that are communicated and enforced are policy that is established and enforced, here conduct standards enforced in code rather than cybersecurity policy alone.

title: Written standards, enforced
why: CIS Controls v8 has no safeguard on written standards of conduct; its awareness safeguards (Control 14) are about training, not about enforcing a code.

title: Roles, background checks and training
outcome: Cybersecurity is included in human resources practices
why: Roles, screening of people with access, and training at hire are the human resources practices this subcategory names.

title: Roles, background checks and training
outcome: Personnel are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform general tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind
why: Security training at hire and every year after is awareness and training for personnel.

title: Roles, background checks and training
outcome: Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, understood, and enforced
why: Defined reporting lines and roles are the established and communicated roles this subcategory covers, which also asks for authorities and enforcement.

title: Roles, background checks and training
outcome: Establish and Maintain a Security Awareness Program
why: An annual training record is evidence of a security awareness program; the criterion also covers roles and screening, which CIS does not address.

title: A current description of the system
outcome: Representations of the organization's authorized network communication and internal and external network data flows are maintained
why: A system map showing parts and connections is a representation of data flows, though the criterion also covers boundaries and who can reach what.

title: A current description of the system
outcome: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained
why: Documenting what the system is covers an inventory of the software, services and systems in it.

title: A current description of the system
outcome: Internal and external threats to the organization are identified and recorded
why: A written threat model naming each kind of actor is a record of internal and external threats.

title: A current description of the system
outcome: Conduct Threat Modeling
why: A threat model that names actors, what each can reach and what bounds it is the threat modeling this safeguard asks for.

title: A current description of the system
outcome: Document Data Flows
why: A system map showing how parts connect documents data flows, though this safeguard is specific to data and the map is not.

title: Telling users what is happening
outcome: Critical objectives, capabilities, and services that external stakeholders depend on or expect from the organization are understood and communicated
why: A status page tells users what the services they depend on are doing, which is communicating those services' state; the subcategory is about the objectives and capabilities themselves.

title: Telling users what is happening
outcome: Internal and external stakeholders are notified of incidents
why: Telling users about incidents that affect them is notifying external stakeholders of incidents.

title: Telling users what is happening
outcome: Define Mechanisms for Communicating During Incident Response
why: A public status page is one mechanism for communicating during an incident, though this safeguard names internal and external channels generally.

title: A risk assessment that repeats
outcome: Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response prioritization
why: Identifying and analyzing risks to the system uses threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods and impacts to prioritize responses.

title: A risk assessment that repeats
outcome: A standardized method for calculating, documenting, categorizing, and prioritizing cybersecurity risks is established and communicated
why: Repeating the assessment as things change needs a standard method to calculate, document and prioritize risk, which the criterion implies.

title: A risk assessment that repeats
outcome: Conduct Threat Modeling
why: CIS has no enterprise risk assessment safeguard; threat modeling is its nearest application-level analog of identifying and analyzing risk.

title: Checking that the controls still work
outcome: Organizational cybersecurity risk management performance is evaluated and reviewed for adjustments needed
why: Evaluating whether controls still function and acting on what is found is evaluating and reviewing risk management performance.

title: Checking that the controls still work
outcome: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events
why: A dashboard sorting each scheduled job into fired, failing or silent monitors software and runtime for adverse events, a narrower sense of the criterion.

title: Checking that the controls still work
outcome: Validate Security Measures
why: Checking that deployed controls still work is validating security measures, though this safeguard sits in a penetration testing Control.

title: Policies deployed as tests
outcome: Secure software development practices are integrated, and their performance is monitored throughout the software development life cycle
why: Policies deployed as tests on every change are secure development practices integrated into the software life cycle.

title: Policies deployed as tests
outcome: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is established based on organizational context, cybersecurity strategy, and priorities and is communicated and enforced
why: A test that fails the build when a policy breaks is how that policy is enforced, not only communicated.

title: Policies deployed as tests
outcome: Implement Code-Level Security Checks
why: Tests on every change that check credentials, route protection and data boundaries are code-level security checks.

title: Least-privilege access
outcome: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties
why: An ordered ladder of access levels with scoped tokens is permissions defined by policy and enforced on least privilege.

title: Least-privilege access
outcome: Define and Maintain Role-Based Access Control
why: Ordered access levels and board-scoped membership are role-based access control defined and maintained.

title: Least-privilege access
outcome: Configure Data Access Control Lists
why: Scoping each shared board to its members is a data access control list, here applied to application records.

title: Reviewing who has access
outcome: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties
why: The criterion's missing piece, a scheduled review of who can reach what, is the reviewed part of this subcategory.

title: Reviewing who has access
outcome: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed by the organization
why: Granting, removing and reviewing access is managing identities and credentials for people, services and hardware.

title: Reviewing who has access
outcome: Establish an Access Granting Process
why: Recording grants is the access granting process this safeguard asks for.

title: Reviewing who has access
outcome: Establish an Access Revoking Process
why: Removing access that is no longer needed is the access revoking process this safeguard asks for.

title: Reviewing who has access
outcome: Disable Dormant Accounts
why: A scheduled review of who has access is how dormant accounts are found and disabled.

title: Credentials encrypted and accounted for
outcome: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed by the organization
why: Encrypted stored credentials, rotated from one screen with a change log, are credentials for services managed by the organization.

title: Credentials encrypted and accounted for
outcome: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected
why: Encrypting stored credentials protects data at rest, for the credential store only.

title: Credentials encrypted and accounted for
outcome: Encrypt Sensitive Data At Rest
why: Encrypting stored credentials with AES-256-GCM is encrypting sensitive data at rest, for the credential store only.

title: Credentials encrypted and accounted for
outcome: Establish and Maintain an Inventory of Service Accounts
why: A ledger of every outside service the site holds a key for resembles an inventory of service accounts, though the ledger lists credentials rather than accounts.

title: Protecting the edges
outcome: Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage
why: Rate limits, sign-in gates and signature checks protect the system from unauthorized use across its network boundary.

title: Protecting the edges
outcome: Identity assertions are protected, conveyed, and verified
why: Verifying inbound webhooks with a constant-time signature comparison is verifying identity assertions.

title: Protecting the edges
outcome: Apply Secure Design Principles in Application Architectures
why: Requiring every writing route to be gated, rate-limited or signature-verified is a secure design principle applied to the application architecture.

title: Encryption in transit
outcome: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit are protected
why: An HTTPS-only response header protects data in transit, as one mechanism rather than a full account of every path.

title: Encryption in transit
outcome: Encrypt Sensitive Data in Transit
why: An HTTPS-only response header is encrypting sensitive data in transit for browsers, as one mechanism.

title: Finding vulnerabilities
outcome: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded
why: Detecting new vulnerabilities in assets is identifying, validating and recording them.

title: Finding vulnerabilities
outcome: Software is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk
why: Dependency updates are software maintained commensurate with risk, the remediation side of the criterion.

title: Finding vulnerabilities
outcome: Establish and Maintain a Vulnerability Management Process
why: Detecting and handling new vulnerabilities is the vulnerability management process this safeguard asks for.

title: Finding vulnerabilities
outcome: Perform Automated Vulnerability Scans of Internal Enterprise Assets
why: Automated scans are the mechanism the criterion names; this safeguard is written for internal assets and a hosted web application is an adaptation.

title: Finding vulnerabilities
outcome: Use Up-to-Date and Trusted Third-Party Software Components
why: Dependency updates are use of up-to-date and trusted third-party software components.

title: Noticing when something breaks
outcome: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events
why: Error reporting and a watcher comparing the live deployment with the latest commit monitor software and runtime for adverse events.

title: Noticing when something breaks
outcome: Information on adverse events is provided to authorized staff and tools
why: Alerts that reach the operator are information on adverse events provided to authorized staff.

title: Noticing when something breaks
outcome: Centralize Security Event Alerting
why: Alerts routed to one operator are security event alerting centralized, at the scale of one person.

title: Responding to incidents
outcome: Incidents are declared when adverse events meet the defined incident criteria
why: A failed check that opens an incident is declaring an incident when an adverse event meets defined criteria.

title: Responding to incidents
outcome: The incident response plan is executed in coordination with relevant third parties once an incident is declared
why: A state machine that carries an incident to resolution is executing an incident response plan, without third-party coordination.

title: Responding to incidents
outcome: Analysis is performed to establish what has taken place during an incident and the root cause of the incident
why: Writing down the lessons from an incident includes establishing what happened and the root cause.

title: Responding to incidents
outcome: Establish and Maintain an Incident Response Process
why: A single state machine from detection to resolution is an incident response process, though the criterion adds containment and lessons.

title: Responding to incidents
outcome: Conduct Post-Incident Reviews
why: The criterion's final step, writing down the lessons, is the post-incident review this safeguard asks for.

title: Every change tested and approved
outcome: Changes and exceptions are managed, assessed for risk impact, recorded, and tracked
why: Changes authorized, tested, approved and recorded before production are changes managed, assessed for risk and tracked.

title: Every change tested and approved
outcome: Configuration management practices are established and applied
why: A pull request gated by lint, tests and a production-matching build is part of how configuration is managed and applied.

title: Every change tested and approved
outcome: Secure software development practices are integrated, and their performance is monitored throughout the software development life cycle
why: Required lint, test and build checks on every change are secure development practices integrated into the life cycle.

title: Every change tested and approved
outcome: Establish and Maintain a Secure Application Development Process
why: A required pull request path with checks is a secure application development process, though v8 has no change management safeguard as such.

title: Every change tested and approved
outcome: Implement Code-Level Security Checks
why: Lint and the full test suite on every change are code-level checks.

title: Vendor risk
outcome: Inventories of services provided by suppliers are maintained
why: A ledger of every outside service the site holds a key for is an inventory of services provided by suppliers.

title: Vendor risk
outcome: The risks posed by a supplier, their products and services, and other third parties are understood, recorded, prioritized, assessed, responded to, and monitored over the course of the relationship
why: Recording every vendor is the first step of understanding and monitoring the risk each poses, which the ledger alone does not do.

title: Vendor risk
outcome: Establish and Maintain an Inventory of Service Providers
why: A complete, test-held vendor list is an inventory of service providers.

title: Backups that restore
outcome: Backups of data are created, protected, maintained, and tested
why: Weekly encrypted, offsite, restore-tested backups are backups created, protected, maintained and tested.

title: Backups that restore
outcome: The integrity of backups and other restoration assets is verified before using them for restoration
why: Restoring into a scratch database and checking the rows verifies backup integrity before real use.

title: Backups that restore
outcome: Perform Automated Backups
why: A scheduled weekly dump of the critical tables is automated backups.

title: Backups that restore
outcome: Protect Recovery Data
why: Encrypting the archive and copying it offsite is protecting recovery data.

title: Backups that restore
outcome: Test Data Recovery
why: Restoring into a scratch database and checking the rows is testing data recovery.

title: Backups that restore
outcome: Establish and Maintain a Data Recovery Process
why: A runbook with recovery targets for each zone is a data recovery process.

title: Capacity and cost limits
outcome: Adequate resource capacity to ensure availability is maintained
why: Rate limits and a spend brake keep demand within what the service can carry, though the subcategory is about capacity itself.

title: Capacity and cost limits
why: CIS Controls v8 has no safeguard on capacity planning or cost limits; its availability coverage is backup and recovery (Control 11).

title: Confidential records walled off
outcome: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties
why: Letting only a client's own module import that client's records enforces access by role on the most sensitive data.

title: Confidential records walled off
outcome: Inventories of data and corresponding metadata for designated data types are maintained
why: Naming which records are confidential and walling them off starts an inventory of designated data types, without the metadata.

title: Confidential records walled off
outcome: Configure Data Access Control Lists
why: A code-level wall around a client's records is an access control list on that data, enforced by test rather than by a file system.

title: Confidential records walled off
outcome: Segment Data Processing and Storage Based on Sensitivity
why: A test-held wall that isolates one client's records from the rest is segmenting data handling by sensitivity.

title: Disposal on a schedule
outcome: Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycles
why: Deleting records after a retention period is managing data through to the end of its life cycle.

title: Disposal on a schedule
outcome: Enforce Data Retention
why: A written retention policy with scheduled deletes is data retention enforced.

title: Disposal on a schedule
outcome: Securely Dispose of Data
why: Deleting records after a period is disposal, though the safeguard also covers how thoroughly data is destroyed.

title: Accurate processing
outcome: Identity assertions are protected, conveyed, and verified
why: Accepting payment webhooks only with a valid signature is verifying identity assertions, one input-integrity check among the criterion's several.

title: Accurate processing
why: Processing integrity (whole-cent money, recomputed figures) is an application correctness concern; CIS v8 has no safeguard on it, and 16.12 code-level checks was considered and rejected as too loose a fit.

title: Notice and choice
outcome: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity - including privacy and civil liberties obligations - are understood and managed
why: A privacy notice and an opt-in analytics cookie respond to privacy obligations; the subcategory is about understanding and managing those obligations.

title: Notice and choice
why: CIS Controls v8 is a security framework with no safeguard on privacy notices or consent; its data safeguards (Control 3) concern protection and handling.
